# t65 - demo-seed product capability: backend/app/scripts/seed_demo.py + the root npm `seed:demo` script (Windows-11-first, Docker banned, no README touch)

## Context

This is the first capability card of `phase_11_readme_demo_seed` (platform issue #71). It adds **one new backend module and one new ROOT npm script line** so that a reviewer or the live demo can log in and see a populated dashboard immediately. It is an operator-directed product capability with **no requirement-id anchor** in the requirements document - its authority is the README live-demo requirement plus the operator directive of 2026-10-15 (precedent: phase_10 was scoped by the directive of 2026-10-14). No new requirement id is invented here, and this card names none in full form anywhere, because on merge it lands where the coverage matrix generator scans citations.

**Binding operator rulings (2026-10-15), encoded as ACs below.** The demo account is FIXED: `demo@example.com` / `demo-password-123`. The seed is an idempotent **wipe-and-rebuild** scoped to that ONE account: a re-run deletes the demo account's demo rows and regenerates deterministic plausible data, and it MUST NOT touch non-demo users. The dataset is roughly 90 days of expenses with a plausible category mix plus budgets for the covered months, and money stays `Decimal` written with exactly 2 decimal places end to end. The existing system-category seed routine is reused, never rewritten: `seed_system_categories(bind)` is imported and called, `seed.py` is frozen.

**Measured ground truth this groom was written against** (all re-measured on this tree at HEAD `04bb2aa`): the ten system categories are already pre-seeded by alembic revision 002, so a fresh migrated probe database holds users=0 and categories=10 - the seed must be idempotent about that rather than assume an empty table. Money columns are `Numeric(12,2)`, which SQLite stores with real/integer affinity, so **money must be verified through the ORM with declared types** (`sa.Numeric`/`sa.Date`): a raw `sqlite3` or untyped `sa.text()` read returns `float`/`str` and would make a 2-dp assertion vacuous - ac3 and ac4 use declared-type Core selects for exactly this reason. UUIDs are stored hex32 (no dashes). The effective dev database is `sqlite:///./dev.db` resolved from `cwd=backend` (no `backend/.env` exists), and `alembic/env.py` builds its engine from the same app settings, so a `DATABASE_URL` override redirects both the migration and the seed - which is what lets every fence run against an isolated probe database under the gitignored `build/` directory and never touch `backend/dev.db`.

**Module contract the builder must satisfy** (the fences measure behaviour; this is the shape they assume). `backend/app/scripts/seed_demo.py` exposes `DEMO_EMAIL`, `DEMO_PASSWORD`, `DEMO_USERNAME`, `SPAN_DAYS = 90`, `RNG_SEED`; `wipe_demo_data(bind)` and `seed_demo_data(bind)` are SQLAlchemy **Core-only and never commit** - `main()` owns the engine and the transaction; the anchor is `date.today()` by default, overridable via `SEED_DEMO_ANCHOR=YYYY-MM-DD`, and generation must be a **pure function of day offset** (an `anchored` dataset whose (offset, category, amount) triple digest is anchor-invariant, which ac6 measures with two different anchors). `main()` must honour the effective `DATABASE_URL` from app settings so the npm invocation can be redirected at a probe database. The wipe leg deletes the demo account's expenses, budgets and audit rows and the demo user row; it must NEVER delete the shared system categories (`user_id` NULL), which every account depends on (ac5 fences that). The ROOT npm line is pinned exactly as `cd backend && uv run python -m app.scripts.seed_demo` so the seed resolves the same settings, `.env` lookup and SQLite path the dev server uses (ac1 matches that contract and rejects anything else).

**File allow-list (4 files, the W5 ceiling).** (1) `backend/app/scripts/seed_demo.py` (new); (2) root `package.json` (the one `seed:demo` line, nothing else); (3) `backend/tests/unit/test_seed_demo.py` (new, the pinned shape/idempotency/isolation node IDs); and (4) **conditional**: `backend/tests/integration/test_seed_demo_api.py` (new) is permitted **only if** the API leg cannot be proven inside file (3) - its trigger is that the login + dashboard assertions need `TestClient` with `dependency_overrides[get_db]`, which the merged t8/t11 integration precedent puts in the integration directory. If the builder can prove ac2's node IDs from the unit file, file (4) must NOT be created and ac2's node IDs move there accordingly; the fences pin node IDs, not the directory choice.

**Contract-first disclosure (read this before the first run).** This card adds the module, so all six fences are **RED at base by design** - each one says so in its own failure text. The positive legs are therefore *measured against a throwaway contract-conforming stub staged temporarily and deleted before this commit* (the t64 `seeded_green_evidence` precedent): with the stub, the module and its two test files staged, all six fences were observed GREEN on this tree, and the handoff records the observed lines. What that proves is that the fences are **satisfiable and non-vacuous** - every fence also carries its own negative control, and each control was observed to bite in the same runs. What it does NOT prove is that the builder's implementation conforms; only the fences do that, at verification time.

**Host facts the operator needs.** `backend/.venv` on this box is WSL-flavoured (`home = /usr/bin`), so `uv run` works from WSL and fails through cmd.exe until `npm run setup:local` has built a win32 venv - ac1 detects the flavour, says which path it took, and measures the same npm script either way, so the gate measures the wiring rather than the venv flavour (the t64 discovered-defect class). No container is used anywhere; nothing here needs docker.

## Acceptance criteria

Six criteria - the W5 maximum for this milestone. Each is one deterministic `bash -c` one-liner carrying its negative control INSIDE the same fence, so a run that prints GREEN also prints the proof that its legs bite. Per-AC state at base and appendability are in the table under **Verification commands**.

## Verification commands

ac_hash: sha256:3103ef0e734942fec913e6edb8b8d9090d0a57c806a214a1d57ddc2def7c12f4

Six fenced commands, byte-identical to `evidence.verification_commands.ac1..ac6` in the groom handoff `docs/state/outputs/t65_definer_groom.json`, and byte-identical to the fenced blocks in **Acceptance criteria** above (this card is composed from the same fence files, so the three copies cannot drift). The `ac_hash` is the sha256 of the `JSON.stringify` of the array of the six trimmed fenced bodies in `ac1..ac6` order, CR-stripped (the t58/t62/t63 recipe), RECOMPUTED from the committed mirror bytes after commit rather than asserted.

Every command is a deterministic single `bash -c` one-liner with exactly two single quotes (the delimiters - no inner single quote anywhere), no heredoc, no backtick, CRLF-tolerant via `tr -d "\r"`, no network and no container. Inline python probes are staged by decoding a base64 payload to `/tmp` and running it under `uv run`: a fence body cannot carry embedded newlines or single quotes, and `printf`-ing a multi-line script with escaped quotes is a known trap (printf does not interpret `\"`), so the base64 channel is the only form that keeps the one-liner contract. Sizes measured with `wc -c` on the CR-stripped bodies: **7194, 5165, 7301, 6191, 8112, 8037 bytes** - all under the 8191-byte Windows CreateProcess ceiling, with ac6 (8037) and ac5 (8112) the tight ones; any future edit to those two must re-measure. Every fence writes only under the gitignored `build/` directory and `/tmp`, and never points the seed at `backend/dev.db` (ac1 asserts the dev.db digest is unchanged by the run).

All six are id-inert: none names a requirement id in full form (ac6 builds its synthetic test id from fragments at runtime precisely so the inertness grep can be proven to bite), and neither this card nor its mirror names one anywhere.

| AC | what it fences | state at base | measured GREEN proof | appendable to the test index? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ac1 | ROOT `package.json` carries the pinned `seed:demo` line (`cd backend && uv run python -m app.scripts.seed_demo`), the module exists, and one `npm run seed:demo` call against an isolated migrated probe database produces exactly one fixed demo account, the ten system categories, >=90 expenses, >=3 budgets and ZERO audit rows - with `backend/dev.db` byte-untouched. Three negative controls: a non-conforming script line, a manifest with no `seed:demo` entry, and an empty-table count. RED at base: the fence names the missing module in its own failure text | observed GREEN with the contract stub + its two test files staged; handoff records the observed evidence lines | yes - deterministic, self-contained, no network, ~1-3 min |

Plus the two pinned node IDs in `backend/tests/integration/test_seed_demo_api.py`. Negative control: a copy with one 1-dp amount and one deleted budget month is REJECTED by the same probe. Appendability is declared per AC; the append decision belongs to the orchestrator at merge, not to this card. **t65 publishes no pin and edits `docs/state/merge_test_index.json` not at all** - the index stays at its 237 measured entries with no stored entry edited (ac6 fences that).

## Out of scope

- **README.md is frozen.** Its digest is pinned by ac6 to the pin-3 document (`f0fd9eda...`, 367 lines). The live-demo prose that names this account belongs to the sibling README cards of this milestone (t66/t67), not here.
- `backend/app/scripts/seed.py`, the ten system categories themselves, and the alembic revision that pre-seeds them: reused, never rewritten.
- `docs/state/merge_test_index.json` (237 entries, no stored entry edited), `backend/scripts/docs_verification.py` (pin custody belongs to t71), `docs/criteria/`, `docs/plan.md`, and the coverage-matrix generator.
- No requirement id is added to the requirements document or the matrix, and no citation is invented for this capability.
- No frontend change, no new endpoint, no schema/migration change, no new dependency, no Makefile or docker target (Docker is banned on this project), no CI change.
- No change to the dev server, auth, or dashboard behaviour: this card only populates rows that the existing endpoints already read.
- `backend/dev.db` and any operator database: the fences never write there.

## Definition of Done

- All six fences run verbatim from the repository root and print GREEN, each in the same run printing its own negative-control line biting (a GREEN without the control line is not a pass).
- `npm run seed:demo` from the repository root is the operator path, works on a win32 venv, and honours `DATABASE_URL` so a probe run cannot write the operator database.
- The builder's diff is confined to the 4-file allow-list (file 4 only if its stated trigger holds); W5: max_files=4, max_acs=6, max_diff_lines 300 (warn-only) - a 90-day generator with two test modules can legitimately exceed 300 lines, which is why the cap stays advisory here.
- mypy stays strict-clean over a surface of at least 91 source files (94 measured with the module and its tests staged), ruff clean, and the full backend suite green on top of the 288 tests carried at grooming.
- Zero changes under every frozen path listed in **Out of scope**; the merge-test index is byte-identical at 237 entries; README keeps the pin-3 digest.
- Card and mirror stay byte-identical and generator-inert; the handoff `docs/state/outputs/t65_definer_groom.json` validates against `definer:groom` and the gate checker passes BEFORE the commit, and the committed files are the bytes that were validated.
- **Discovered defects (recorded, not fixed here - fixing them would be another card's work):** (1) `backend/.venv` is WSL-flavoured on this box, so `npm run seed:demo` through cmd.exe cannot work until `npm run setup:local` rebuilds a win32 venv; ac1 detects and reports which path it measured instead of silently passing. (2) A raw `sqlite3`/untyped-`text()` read of the money and date columns returns `float`/`str`, so any future money gate that skips declared Core types is vacuous by construction - the reason ac3/ac4/ac6 read through `sa.Numeric`/`sa.Date`.
